newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank says no gold sales planned.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank says no gold sales planned.

text.p: Taiwan central bank vice governor Hsu Chia-tung said on Friday the bank had reviewed possible changes in its gold reserve policy in line with other central banks but had no plans to sell gold now.
"We have had some internal review of how we might change our gold reserve policy," Hsu said. "But right now this cannot be implemented."
Hsu said a major recent gold selloff by the Australian central bank was one factor prompting Taiwan's bank to review its policy on gold reserves.
"There are some voices within the (Taiwan) central bank suggesting that we should make some changes," he said.
Hsu, speaking at a regular news conference, said any sale of gold by Taiwan would have to take into consideration the prevailing price and market conditions.
"If we were to consider selling down our gold reserves, we must take the right timing," he said. "Considering that the gold price is low right now, we don't consider the timing to be right."
Taiwan had 13.565 million troy ounces at the end of March, up from 13.553 million ounces in November, according to the most recent figures from the central bank.

The central bank's decision to stay its gold reserve policy was in line with expectations of local gold traders, who have said Australia's heavy selling might motivate other central banks to sell -- but not Taiwan's.
"The Australian central bank's new gold reserve policy may start another round of government selling," a gold trader at Taiwan's China Trust Bank said.
"Taiwan's long-time policy is to hold its gold reserves."
Local Taiwan gold demand has risen sharply as the price has slipped to 12-year lows.

Traders estimated demand from Taiwan's jewellery industry had risen about 20 percent since late June, while investors' buying had jumped about 50 percent in the past five days alone, a leading dealer at Taiwan's Central Trust of China said.
Jewellery manufacturing creates the bulk of Taiwan demand.
The world gold price took another hit on Thursday after the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves in a change of reserves philosophy.
Australia is the world's third-largest gold producer.
The Canadian and Brazilian central banks have shown similar policy shifts and reduced their gold reserves.
